errors.text: The proposed W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V and Nb-Mo-Ta-W compositions contain Group VI elements and do not reconstruct the targeted Group IV-V HfNbTaTiZr alloy family.
Laser powder-bed fusion followed by generic annealing replaces the central ink-extrusion, hydrogen de-binding, vacuum-sintering, oxygen-gettering, and water-quenching route.
The hypothesis treats interstitials as impurities to minimize, whereas the target relies on controlled oxygen uptake near 1 wt.% for interstitial strengthening.

Annealing is asserted to reduce interstitial concentration or ordered-complex effects without a specified scavenging, degassing, or phase-control mechanism; the cited evidence does not establish this claim.
The critical cooling-rate dependence, metastable beta-BCC retention by quenching, hydride decomposition sequence, and oxidation-resistant silicide coating are omitted.
